candidate.answerReason: The exits are 120 miles apart. Three-fourths of that distance is 90 miles, and 40 + 90 = 130.

methods.label: Find three-fourths of the distance
methods.explanation:
The fraction describes the distance between the two exits, so first find that distance:
\[
160-40=120\text{ miles}.
\]
Three-fourths of this distance is
\[
\frac34\cdot120=90\text{ miles}.
\]
Starting at milepost \(40\) and traveling \(90\) miles toward milepost \(160\) puts the service center at \(40+90=130\). The answer is milepost \(130\), choice \(\text{E}\).
methods.levelReason: The method uses whole-number subtraction and addition together with a fraction of an integer.

candidate.annotationRationale: The central target is applying a fractional part to the distance between two mileposts. Fraction-by-integer multiplication supports the calculation; fraction-by-fraction multiplication and equal exit spacing are unnecessary.
